 LPG cylinder costs Rs 10,000 in Pakistan as border closure triggers shortages, 6,000 dealer shops shut
 SECTIONS LPG cylinder costs Rs 10,000 in Pakistan as border closure triggers shortages, 6,000 dealer shops shut By Trending Desk , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 25, 2026, 07:56:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Pakistan's LPG crisis has pushed prices to Rs 750 per kilogram in some areas, taking cylinder costs above Rs 10,000. The Gabd-Rimdan crossing with Iran has reopened after a week-long suspension, but dealers are protesting alleged harassment by enforcement agencies. With market rates far above the official price, households are struggling to secure affordable cooking fuel.
 ANI LPG cylinder costs Rs 10,000 in Pakistan as border closure triggers shortages, 6,000 shops shut Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices have surged to as much as Rs 750 per kilogram in parts of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, pushing cylinder costs above Rs 10,000 as supply disruptions linked to the closure of a key border crossing with Iran triggered shortages and concerns over profiteering. The price spike has hit households already facing limited access to natural gas, while LPG dealers across the country have shut thousands of shops in protest against alleged harassment by enforcement agencies and what they describe as the authorities' failure to act against companies accused of overcharging consumers, according to Pakistani media reports.
 Pakistan has now reopened the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing with Iran in Balochistan's Gwadar district after a week-long suspension disrupted trade, stranded freight vehicles and heightened concerns over LPG supplies ahead of winter. Commercial consignments accompanied by consignment notes dated October 16 or earlier were allowed to cross when trade operations resumed on Saturday, Dawn reported. However, the reopening comes amid an ongoing LPG supply and pricing crisis.

 LPG dealers shut shops over alleged harassment
Thousands of LPG retailers across Pakistan have suspended operations to protest alleged harassment by enforcement agencies and the government's failure to take effective action against LPG companies and sellers accused of profiteering, The Express Tribune reported.
Approximately 5,500 to 6,000 LPG shops have closed in Lahore and several other cities, leaving consumers searching for outlets with available supplies. The shutdown follows days of exceptionally high LPG prices and has added to the difficulties faced by households struggling with rising living costs.
 Live Events
 Shopkeeper Kashif Bilal Asghar alleged that personnel from the PERA Force and Civil Defence had confiscated LPG filling equipment from retailers. He said the pumps cost between Pakistani rupees (PKR) 50,000 and PKR 60,000 each, while shopkeepers faced fines ranging from PKR 5,000 to PKR 10,000.
 Asghar accused the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) of failing to hold LPG companies and plants accountable for alleged profiteering, claiming that enforcement actions were instead focused on small retailers. Dealers say continued penalties and financial losses have left them with little choice but to suspend business.
 The strike has further restricted access to cooking gas, forcing some households to turn to coal and dry firewood to meet their daily cooking needs.
 LPG prices far exceed official rates
According to The Express Tribune, LPG prices have risen sharply over the past five to six days amid declining supplies, reportedly linked to the closure of the Taftan border following tensions between Iran and the United States.
A senior OGRA official said Pakistan imports nearly 70% of its LPG requirements, while domestic production accounts for the remaining 30%.
Despite OGRA fixing the official LPG price at Rs 279.34 per kilogram for the current month, consumers in several markets have been paying between Rs 550 and Rs 600 per kilogram. Prices in Peshawar have reached around Rs 600 per kilogram, while some northern areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have reported rates as high as Rs 750.
At these prices, the cost of a cylinder can exceed Rs 10,000, placing additional pressure on households that depend on LPG for cooking.

 Regulator yet to begin proposed crackdown
OGRA has not yet initiated its proposed crackdown against companies and sellers accused of overcharging consumers. Officials reportedly fear that enforcement measures could trigger further strikes, disrupt distribution and aggravate the country's energy shortages.
An OGRA official warned that prices in affected markets could rise beyond Rs 700 per kilogram if supply disruptions intensify.
An OGRA spokesperson acknowledged that the Taftan border closure had created supply challenges but said efforts were under way to stabilise the situation. The spokesperson expressed optimism that the crisis would be brought under control soon, The Express Tribune reported.
 Low-income households face growing hardship
The LPG price surge has particularly affected low-income families in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where shortages of natural gas have compounded the problem. Residents in rural areas and settlements around Peshawar are increasingly turning to firewood as LPG becomes unaffordable and piped gas remains scarce.
With dealers protesting, supplies disrupted and market prices far above the official rate, households face additional uncertainty over access to cooking fuel. Although the reopening of the Gabd-Rimdan crossing has resumed some trade with Iran, the immediate impact on LPG availability and prices remains unclear.
